messages:
ana-ml: Quick spin on separating prefill vs decode batchers + phase-aware token budgets. Ran on canary with 8xA100, mixed prompt lengths. TL;DR: p99 short-prompt latency down ~12%, but end-to-end throughput dipped ~6% on steady 40-token streams. attaching config and perf snippets.

mike-runtime: Can you paste the exact batcher config and token_budget targets? curious if kernel selection changed with the split.

ana-ml: oops typo, ana-ml: pasted below — we left kernel selection unchanged (auto), just adjusted batching heuristics and added a phase flag to the scheduler.

ana-ml: ```
# split-batcher config (canary)
batcher.prefill.enabled = true
batcher.decode.enabled = true
batcher.prefill.max_batch_tokens = 4096
batcher.decode.max_batch_tokens = 2048
batcher.phase_budget.prefill = 0.6  # fraction of in-flight token budget
batcher.phase_budget.decode = 0.35
batcher.kv_drain.timeout_ms = 6
# note: kernel_selector.mode = auto
```

syl: interesting. Did you see KV cache drain spikes during handoff? if decode queue stalls while prefill spikes, KV eviction thrash could kill throughput.

ana-ml: yes, good catch. The profiler shows periodic KV drain peaks aligned with prefill bursts. I instrumented the KV drain time histogram — 95th jumped from 2ms -> 12ms during the run.

raj: can you attach flame/trace from the runtime perf traces? need to check if the GPU kernels are spending more time waiting on kv_lock or memcpy. also run the new kernel sampling (kernel_selector.debug=1) to see any shifts to slower matmul kernels.

ana-ml: attached short export (snippet):
```
TRACE: phase=prefill batch_id=4321 kv_drain=11.8ms kernel_wait=2.1ms matmul_kernel=cuBLAS_v2::sgemm_fast
TRACE: phase=decode batch_id=4322 kv_drain=2.2ms kernel_wait=3.0ms matmul_kernel=custom_mm_q4
```

mike-runtime: Hmm that shows prefill suffering from KV drain much more. If prefill is allowed big token budget (0.6) it monopolizes KV accesses. Maybe add a KV backoff: reduce prefill phase_budget when kv_drain > X ms.

ana-ml: I prototyped a simple adaptive backoff: if kv_drain_95 > 8ms then prefill_budget *= 0.75 and decode_budget += 0.15. With that, throughput restored ~3% and p99 stayed ~8% better than baseline.

raj: Nice. Did you measure model quality (sampling differences) after forcing decode to smaller batches? we should ensure no sampling bias introduced by batcher ordering.

ana-ml: Checked basic sampling seeds for generation, no statistically significant divergence on our eval set. will run full eval.

ops-bot: CI canary deploy 1772506012 -> started. integration tests queued. :rocket:

ana-ml: Plan: 1) add KV-drain adaptive backoff heuristic, 2) add kernel_selector.debug logging to canary for next 48h, 3) run full eval set for regens, 4) canary metrics dashboard (p50/p95/p99, throughput, kv_drain_hist, kernel_switch_count).

mike-runtime: one more ask — add a fallback policy: if throughput drops >10% for 10m, revert to unified batcher automatically. avoid prolonged regressions.

ana-ml: +1. I'll add revert rule to rollout config.

syl: also add a small spike test: synthetic burst of small prompts to validate tail behavior. earlier runs missed that scenario.

ana-ml: will do. tagging @taylor-sre for canary alert thresholds.

taylor-sre: thanks — set alert: canary_throughput_drop > 8% sustained for 5m => page. canary_p99_increase > 15% for 5m => page. also collect kernel_switch_count as a metric but no page, just dashboard.

ana-ml: Thanks all. Next update after 24h of canary + full eval. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
